messages:
ada_sales: Heads-up — PulseMed wants a HIPAA POC with reserved capacity. They estimate baseline ~350 qps, morning window spikes up to ~1400 qps (avg ~90 tokens), spikes last ~4-8m. Need sizing, preheat plan, autoscale snippet, and an SLA blurb for SOW by Tues.

ryan_eng: Noted. Quick clarifier: are spikes predictable daily events or ad-hoc? Predictability affects preheat strategy.

ada_sales: Mostly predictable (08:15 local) but with occasional ad-hoc surges. They want a firm p99 target on reserved resources.

ryan_eng: Ballpark perf: our x-hyper nodes with int8 quantized can do ~320 qps/GPU @90 tokens. For 1400 peak I'd recommend reserving 5 GPUs and allowing 2 burst credits for short spikes. That gives headroom and smoother autoscale.

maya_sre: Agree on 5 reserved + 2 burst. KV shards = 10 (2 shards per GPU) to avoid hot keys. Recommend AZ spread across 3 AZs and a staggered preheat starting 25m before expected peak to warm both weights and KV.

leo_prod: Fallback plan: a compact model (gpt-compact-int8) for degraded mode to preserve availability with p99 up to ~450-650ms. Routing priority: reserved -> burst_pool -> degraded_shared. We'll instrument quality checks while fallback active.

henry_ops: Ops controls: global_rate_limit: 1600qps, max_queue_depth: 800. Add fair-queueing by customer token to avoid single-tenant hogging. Also enable shedding policy: shed lowest-priority non-authenticated requests first.

ada_sales: Can someone give a short preheat command and an autoscale snippet I can paste into the SOW?

maya_sre: Preheat example (single-line for docs):

redwood preheat --project pulsemed-poc --model gpt-med-int8 --shards 10 --duration 25m --warm_weights true --preheat-stagger 60s

ryan_eng: Autoscale snippet for SOW (YAML, simple):

autoscale:
  reserved_gpus: "5"
  burst_credits: "2"
  preheat_minutes: "25"
  kv_shards: "10"
  az_spread: "3"
  scale_up:
    policy: "fast"
    target_util_percent: "60"
    cooldown_seconds: "15"
  scale_down:
    policy: "controlled"
    grace_seconds: "300"
  degraded_model: "gpt-compact-int8"

maya_sre: SLA language we can return: "When serving from reserved capacity (reserved_gpus=5) with KV warmed and no evictions, Redwood commits to p99 latency < 250ms. If requests are served from burst credits or degraded model, p99 may increase up to 450-650ms; SOW will include measured fallbacks and rollback triggers."

legal_claire: For HIPAA we need the questionnaire, acceptance of our BAA, KMS envelope encryption, VPC peering/PrivateLink option, audit logs >=90 days, and SOC reports. Ada please forward their security packet.

henry_ops: Cost note for presales: reserved 5 GPUs monthly commit + burst credits billed pay-as-you-go. For a 30-day POC, ballpark = reserved baseline + variable burst usage; ops will provide a rough $/day estimate offline.

leo_prod: Runbook triggers: if p99 > 300ms for 90s -> trigger alert; if sustained > 400ms for 2m -> rollback to degraded_model and notify customer. Also include manual override to disable preheat if they want cost savings.

scheduler-bot: Placeholder preheat scheduled: pulsemed-poc / preheat / 2025-01-08T08:50Z :calendar:

ada_sales: Perfect — I'll assemble the SOW bundle with reserved_gpus:5, burst_credits:2, preheat:25m, SLA caveat, runbook summary, and send to PulseMed. Will DM legal with their questionnaire. Thanks all :raised_hands:
